title: 4.5-Year Follow-up with a Novel Corneal Endothelial Prosthesis

indication: Chronic corneal edema from endothelial failure in eyes with low visual potential or complex anterior/posterior segment pathology (complicated cataract surgery with vitrectomy or Artisan lenses, pseudophakic bullous keratopathy, angle-closure glaucoma in nanophthalmos, Fuchs dystrophy after Descemet removal, failed keratoplasties); 7 eyes in the first-in-human trial, 3 later eyes

groups.description: Implantation of the EndoArt (EyeYon Medical), a 6.5 mm dome-shaped 50-µm acrylic endothelial prosthesis placed against the posterior cornea as a fluid barrier, with air tamponade; rebubbling as needed; anchoring sutures (removed after 4 weeks) introduced from case 4 onwards; Amsterdam UMC, single surgeon team, technique developed during the series; 10 eyes of 10 patients

exclusions.reason: Only the undated 'Last postop' follow-up; the preoperative cell is also digit-grouped and above the validator's 1300 µm reference limit; device adherence failed and re-PKP was advised at 6 months
Only the undated 'Last postop' follow-up column; no dated follow-up

exclusions.what: TB0429-1 column C3 'Last postop (microns)' for all patients

exclusions.reason: Group summaries; per-eye rows exist, so individual series are used (protocol: group means only when no per-eye rows exist)

exclusions.what: CCT values in the case descriptions, Abstract mean CCT and Figure 3 (mean CCT over time)
exclusions.reason: Text and figure values, not table cells

exclusions.what: Tables 2 and 3 (rebubbles, sutures, success/fail, visual acuity)

notes: Role treated: the EndoArt is a novel investigational endothelial prosthesis (first-in-human trial for cases 1-7; cases 8-10 implanted after the device became available); single-arm series without a comparator. Procedure context 'other' (synthetic endothelial barrier, not a tissue endothelial keratoplasty).
Per-eye rows exist, so each eye is an individual series (n = 1); Table 1 columns are labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4 years without exact visit dates.
CCT measurement method is not named (case 4 mentions the thinnest point 'in topography'; Figure 2 is an OCT image); method recorded as 'unstated'.
Case-description CCT values for patients 5, 8 and 9 do not match their Table 1 entries; Table 1 cells are cited (these three eyes are not in the record).

The surgical technique changed during the series (sutures from case 4, multiple rebubbles in early cases). The article processing charge was funded by the device manufacturer; the corresponding author declares consulting for the manufacturer.

Patients 1 and 5 were added by the developer after the thickness builder learned to read thin/hair-space thousands separators (digit-group rule); the extractor had excluded them only for that parsing reason.
